facts.statement: The type species Macroplata tenuiceps is known from a nearly complete skeleton found in the Blue Lias Formation of Harbury, Warwickshire, UK.
facts.quote: It is known from a nearly complete skeleton NHMUK PV R 5488 (formerly BMNH R 5488) from the Blue Lias Formation (Hettangian) of Harbury, Warwickshire, UK.

facts.statement: Macroplata likely fed on fish using its sharp, needle-like teeth.
facts.quote: Like other plesiosaurs, Macroplata probably lived on a diet of fish, using its sharp needle-like teeth to catch prey.

facts.statement: Large shoulder bones suggest Macroplata used powerful forward strokes to swim fast.
facts.quote: Its shoulder bones were fairly large, indicating a powerful forward stroke for fast swimming.

facts.statement: Macroplata possessed a relatively long neck that was twice the length of its skull, unlike pliosaurs.
facts.quote: Macroplata also had a relatively long neck, twice the length of the skull, in contrast to pliosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype and only known specimen is a nearly complete skeleton named BMNH R5488, discovered in Warwickshire, England.
facts.quote: cuyo holotipo y único espécimen conocido es un esqueleto casi completo denominado como BMNH R5488, descubierto en el condado de Warwickshire en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The name Macroplata means "big plate" and it is an extinct genus represented by a single basal rhomaleosaurid plesiosaurid species.
facts.quote: Macroplata (nombre que significa "lámina grande") es un género extinto representado por una única especie de pliosauroide romaleosáurido basal

facts.statement: Macroplata lived in the Early Jurassic in the UK and grew up to 5 meters long.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Jurásico inferior en el Reino Unido, que llegaba a crecer hasta 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Macroplata belongs to the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Macroplata is classified within the suborder Pliosauroidea.
Macroplata is estimated to have been between 4.38 and 4.65 meters in body length and weighed approximately 604 kilograms.
facts.quote: Macroplata is estimated around 4.38 - 4.65 m in body length and 604 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: The better-preserved maxilla of the holotype has 18 tooth sockets, with the smallest located at the back.
facts.quote: The better-preserved maxilla of the holotype bears 18 alveoli (tooth sockets), with the smallest at the back.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the size of the pineal foramen in Macroplata, with sources claiming it was both large and small.
facts.quote: Upon the discovery of Macroplata, its pineal foramen was claimed to be both large and small by different sources.

facts.statement: The species Macroplata longirostris was reclassified in 2011 as a pliosaurid in the genus Hauffiosaurus.
facts.quote: A different species, Macroplata longirostris (previously called Plesiosaurus longirostris), which lived somewhat later, during the Toarcian stage, was also included in the genus; however, in 2011, Benson et al. reclassified it as a pliosaurid in the genus Hauffiosaurus, H. longirostris.
